chief_complaint: Uncontrolled stage 2 hypertension in the setting of obesity, prediabetes, and obstructive sleep apnea
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 37-year-old male with a history of obesity (BMI >=30) diagnosed in 2017, prediabetes since 2007 (A1c 5.9%), anemia since 2007, and obstructive sleep apnea diagnosed in late 2018. Blood pressure measured most recently at 169/105 mmHg meets criteria for stage 2 hypertension. He reports ongoing intimate partner abuse since early 2019 and works part‑time, indicating socioeconomic stressors. The last documented encounter was in February 2019; since then no antihypertensive, glucose‑lowering, or sleep‑apnea therapies have been recorded. He is currently taking diphenhydramine 25 mg PRN for an unspecified indication, which may worsen sleep quality. Overall, his clinical trajectory shows escalating cardiovascular and metabolic risk with minimal pharmacologic intervention and significant psychosocial barriers.

Organ systems at elevated risk: cardiovascular (elevated BP, obesity, OSA), metabolic (prediabetes, obesity), renal (uncontrolled BP, unknown eGFR), hematologic (anemia), respiratory (sleep apnea), and mental health/social (intimate partner violence, socioeconomic stress).
